docs.title: Anonymising your work
docs.text:
Anonymising Your Work You may need to anonymise your work before submitting summative assignments; the VLE won't do this for you. This page gives you instructions on how to turn word documents, pdfs, and ppts into anonymous formats ready to submit.

Anonymising Your WorkRemoving metadata from your fileAssessment guides

Anonymising Your Work For anonymous summative assignments, you will need to anonymise your files before submitting. It is your responsibility to ensure your name, exam number, and any other personally identifiable information does not appear on your file. This includes:

The file name - ensure you rename it to something that doesn't identify you The file contents - do not include your name or exam number anywhere in the file The file metadata - such as 'author name' or 'last modified by'. Removing metadata from your file On a windows computer for word, excel, or powerpoint: Open the document you want to anonymise

On the file tab, select info Select check for issues, and then 'inspect document' Select the areas you want to check for author information, then click 'inspect' Select 'remove all'. Save the file. For more information, you can follow these instructions.

On a mac computer for word or excel: Go to Tools > Protect Document, and check the box "Remove personal information from this file on save". Then save the file.

For powerpoint: File > Properties, and manually delete any identifying information in the fields on the summary tab, and the 'properties' box of the custom tab. Save the file.

When creating a pdf: If you are converting something into a pdf, you can anonymise it as you convert. Click on 'more options' in the Save As menu, then:

Delete all content out of the Author’s field beneath the Save as Type dropdown. The field is editable if you click on it. Click on the Options button. Untick box by Document Properties. Click OK. Click save. Anonymising an existing pdf: Open the file within Corel PDF Fusion (available on all IT Classroom PCs).

Click on the Document menu option, then pick Document Settings from the menu list that appears. Ensure you’re on the Summary tab (this is the one you should be on by default). Delete all content out of the Author field. Click OK. docs.title: Submitting assignments
docs.text:
Submitting assignments on the VLE Written assignments like essays and reports are usually via the module's Learn Ultra (Blackboard) VLE site. Submission points will usually be located in the Assessment section of the module site.

There are three main types of submission points:

Ultra Assignment Turnitin Gradescope Find out more about each in the boxes below.

General assignment submission adviceLearn Ultra AssignmentsTurnItIn AssignmentsVideo & audio submissionsGradescope AssignmentsAssessment guides

General assignment submission advice For any assignment, make sure to:

find out where the submission point is far in advance of the deadline. submit assignments on a computer. Don't submit assignments on a mobile device. read the guidelines carefully - check the deadline, file type requirements and other information so you know what you need to do. anonymise your work appropriately (see our specific guide on how to do this). These guides are relevant to most assessment submissions via the VLE:

Google DocSubmitting Assignments on the VLE General advice on submitting VLE assignments. Google DocUrgent Help With Submission Issues (Troubleshooting) Quick tips for dealing with issues when trying to submit something to the VLE. thumbsup sign in a speech bubbleAssessment and Feedback What markers are looking for in your work and using feedback to improve your writing. Learn Ultra Assignments Ultra Assignments:

are usually used for digital written work (ie. typed), but can also be scans of handwritten work, slides etc. can be used for video and audio files - see the specific video & audio submissions guidance are mostly used for Formative assignments (useful for developmental feedback on your work), but can be used for non-anonymous Summative assignments (count for a grade). can be used for individual and group assessments usually have an that icon looks like a cartoon checklist with a black outline. decorative

Make sure that you make note of any specific instructions from your department, eg. which file type to use, if you can/should upload multiple files, file orientation etc.

See the demonstration video and detailed written guide below for instructions on how to submit your work.

docs.title: Troubleshooting common issues
docs.text:
Summary

Quickly solve many general issues yourself by completing standard troubleshooting steps.

docs.title: Which issues can this fix?
docs.text:
Many general issues with our systems (particularly Learn Ultra and Panopto) can be easily and quickly solved with these steps, including:

  • content not loading
  • changes not saving
  • errors for something that usually works

If you're contacting us for help with issues like this, please try these steps first to see if they fix your problem. We'll ask you to do them first anyway!

docs.title: Key troubleshooting steps
docs.text:
1. Use a supported and up to date browser (Chrome or Firefox)
  2. Clear cookies & cache
  3. Disable browser extensions/add-ons
  4. Enable pop ups
  5. Consider cookie settings

For more information on how to complete these steps, see our troubleshooting guide (also embedded below).

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Getting started with Replay (Panopto) Replay is the main way that tutors create video content for your modules - this might be lecture recordings, demonstrations, feedback on sessions or other useful content.

Panopto is the software that plays these videos (usually through a module's VLE site). It has features to help you study effectively, like notes, bookmarks and searches.

Useful guides Google DocReplay/Panopto student guide Using Replay/Panopto to view lecture captures in the browser and the Panopto app. Replay-Panopto Student Guides A playlist of bite-size guides to Panopto's features. Accessing Replay Recordings There are a few different ways to access Replay recordings:

Access all of a module's videos using the Replay Lecture Capture (Panopto) link in the module site's Course Content area. Individual videos may also be linked individually or embedded in the relevant materials section. You can also use the Panopto app to access module recordings. Peplay Lecture Capture link shown in course content list

Watching Replay Recordings There are different ways to watch Panopto recordings:

In a VLE site's Replay Content folder, click the video's title to open it in the Panopto video player. For a video embedded in a VLE module page (like the ones on this page), click the triangle icon to play. You can use the icons in the bottom right to open it in the Panopto video player, or to watch in full screen. If you're using the Blackboard app, you might need to log in before watching a video - do this with your usual University username and password. On a mobile device, you can watch videos using the Panopto app (see below). If you have problems accessing videos, try logging into Panopto [Webpage] directly, then refreshing your VLE page.

You can adjust various settings in the Panopto video player, such as playback speed and captions.

Features of the Panopto video viewer Learn about the features of Panopto’s interactive viewer. Accessibility features in Panopto Including screenreader support, keyboard navigation and captions.

Playback in Replay [YouTube video]

Get the most out of Panopto's features If you watch a video in the Panopto player, you can access useful features to help you study effectively and interact with other students.

To access them, open the video the Panopto and you'll find them on the left of the Panopto video player.

You can Search for words that appear in the video, to help you find the information you need. Notes are personal to you and can't be seen by other students. Bookmarks are reminders so you can find a point quickly again (these are also personal to you). You can see your bookmarks in all videos by clicking the 'See all your bookmarks link. Discussions let you post comments and questions that can be seen by everyone who can access the video. This space is for students to learn collaboratively - your lecturer won't answer questions posted here. How to use Panopto video search Search the video library for a video and search inside a video. How to create and access Panopto bookmarks Add time-stamped bookmarks to videos to easily go back to specific sections later. Replay/Panopto guides Getting started with Replay/Panopto Studying with Replay/Panopto Panopto app Accessibility tips: video and audio Having problems? Use the right browser Use Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox, or use the Panopto app.

Use the correct version We have two versions of Replay/Panopto:

one for Learn Ultra VLE (most courses) one for York Online programmes. Make sure you log into the right version! Find out more in this guide:

Google DocPanopto: log into the correct version Make sure you're using the Learn Ultra VLE version or the York Online version. Still having problems? See our Troubleshooting guide for more things to try:

docs.title: Blackboard app
docs.text:
Using the Blackboard App The blackboard app allows you to access the VLE from your mobile device, and do things such as checking course content and contribute to discussions. It is not recommended to use the Blackboard App for any assessment-related activity, such as checking grades or submitting assessments.

The Blackboard AppSetting up the Blackboard AppNavigating the Blackboard AppWhen to use the Blackboard App?Learn Ultra VLE guides

The Blackboard App You can use the Blackboard app to access the VLE on a mobile device:

Blackboard app for iOS [Webpage] Blackboard app for Android [Webpage] The app is useful for quickly checking course content, announcements and participating in Discussion Forums.

Don't use the Blackboard app for any assessment activity!

Setting up the Blackboard App Once you have installed the app, you need to log in to be able to access the VLE.

Enter University of York (not York University, that's in Canada) into the 'type your school/workspace name' field Tap the Log in / Continue with Web-Login button (changes depending on your device type) Enter your VLE log in information (eg username abc123) Tap Log in Duo two-factor authentication This is a series of screenshots from the Blackboard app demonstrating the steps detailed above. The screenshots show entering University of York into the school name field, clicking 'log in', entering log in information, and the duo two factor authentication notification.

You can now access the VLE through the Blackboard app.

Navigating the Blackboard App Click a module from the Courses page on the bottom of the screen to open its Course Materials page, containing Announcements, Course Content and other items. The Course Content page is the equivalent of the left hand menu on the browser site (items might appear in a different order) - choose the area you want to look at. To go back, use the back arrow at the top left of the screen or the usual back function on your mobile.

Find out more:

Google docGetting Started with the Blackboard AppThis link opens in a new window When to use the Blackboard App? Quickly checking course content and announcements Reading and responding to discussions Adding to a journal Don't use the Blackboard App for: Assessments - including checking due dates, assignment details, grades/feedback, taking tests, and submitting assignments. Panopto - use the panopto app instead, or use google chrome or mozilla firefox on mobile to watch lecture recordings. Reading lists - use google chrome or mozilla firefox instead. It is not recommended that you use the mobile app for any assessment related activity. Mobile app updates can disrupt functionality of these with little warning, and so the mobile app should not be used for important activity such as assessments.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Navigating the Ultra system The main site navigation bar appears on the left hand side on a larger screen, or can be accessed through the three lines icon in the top left on a smaller screen.

Navigation menu: described in text below

Use the menu to navigate between:

Your profile: manage your notification settings, avatar and personal information Home: landing page with key system updates and departmental links Activity: summary of activity collated across all your sites Courses: access your module and other academic-related sites Communities: access your non-academic sites, such as departmental noticeboards. If you are not enrolled on any Community sites, this option will not appear. Calendar: collates Due Dates across all your sites. Does not integrate with the Timetable or other UoY systems. Messages: summary of Messages (announcements for specific students) in your sites. These are not used much, and you may not see this item in your menu. Marks: summary of assessments and marks received across your sites Tools: access to some LTIs - it's not likely you'll need this page. Your current page is highlighted in the menu.

Courses & Communities pages: access your sites The Courses page lists all your module sites and other academic-related sites such as the Academic Integrity Tutorial and Turnitin Tutorial. The Communities page lists non-academic sites, like student noticeboard or departmental careers sites. Both pages work in the same way.

You can customise the pages in a number of ways:

Layout: select list or grid layout (grid layout contains image thumbnails)

Search courses by module/site name or keyword

Terms: select a specific academic year

Filters: various course types (which aren't used at UoY)

Items per page: Show 25, 50 or 100 sites per page

Favourite your modules: click the star icon to pin to the top of the default all sites list and any applicable search/filter results.

Navigating Ultra sites General site navigation Module site showing Content page. Menu above the banner, site content in the main section. Further described in text. Use the navigation bar at the top to move between different parts of the site:

Content: the site homepage, where all your module content is found. This also shows the module teaching staff. Calendar: Due Dates for assessments within the site. Note! This does not integrate with the Timetable or other UoY systems. Announcements: updates from module staff. Discussions: any discussions in the site, including any just for your specific group. Gradebook: collates all assessments in the site. Groups: details of any groups you are in for collaborative work. You can also use this navigation bar to move between different sites or system areas:

Home: to close the site and return to the Courses page. Courses: course switcher to move between recently-visited or favourite course sites. Site sections In most cases, sites should contain the following key sections:

Module information: an overview of the module, staff contact details, accessibility info and where to get help Assessment: all the assessment information for the module Reading List: containing all assigned reading for the module Replay Lecture Capture (Panopto): the site's lecture capture recordings Module materials: usually in weekly sections Navigating content items Most items should be organised within folders. Click a folder to show the content within it, and then click an item to open it.

Described in text

Once you open an item, a breadcrumb trail appears in the top bar to show the item's location in the site. Note that the folder links aren't clickable. Click the X button to close the item and return to your previous location.

For most folder types, there is a collapsible Contents panel to quickly jump to a specific item, and Previous / Next arrows in the top right to move between items. To help you focus, these disappear if you start an assessment attempt.

Described in text

Search You can also Search for content items. Click the magnifying glass icon above the course content and type into the search box. Matching items will appear as you type.

Described in text

docs.title: POTATOES
docs.text:
Each module has a Learn Ultra VLE site containing content like:

module materials: lecture slides, reading lists, quizzes etc. access to lecture recordings. assignment submission points and online exams. interactive tools for discussion and collaborative work. You'll also find other important sites like the Academic Integrity Tutorial, Turnitin training and academic skills support.

Learn Ultra VLEThis link opens in a new window Access the VLE using this link or by going to vle.york.ac.uk at any time. Note: York Online programmes use the Canvas VLE, which has its own guidance

Introduction video This video covers logging in, general navigation, changing notification settings, and accessing feedback, lecture recordings, and reading lists.

Blackboard Learn - Navigation (Students) [YouTube]

Some aspects of the navigation are a little out-of-date now; see the Navigating Ultra page for updated advice.

Navigating UltraThis link opens in a new window VLE top tips Favourite your modules, search your sites, download the app Favourite your modules so they appear at the top of your Courses list. Use the Search feature on your module sites to quickly locate items, even if they are in folders. Use the mobile app and view or listen to your resources on the go. Alternative formats can be useful in different ways. Announcements & the Activity Stream Lecturers often send course updates and other important information through Blackboard Learn Announcements.

Within an individual module site, Announcements is often a module's homepage. You can also open the Announcements from the module's left hand menu.

You can also access Announcements from all your sites in one place in the Activity Stream.

Notification list including upcoming assignment submission date, today's notification about reading list, and recent announcement and marks posting.

The Activity Stream also has other notifications from sites, such as:

new materials or sites due dates in the next seven days marks posted for assessments within Blackboard Find out more about Activity Stream and adapting your notification settings:

Activity Stream Blackboard's guide to what you can see in the Activity Stream.

Notification settings Blackboard's guide to adapting what you receive notifications about and how.
